# Song of Solomon Chapter 6 -- The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** "Where has your beloved gone, O woman of rare beauty? Which way did he turn so we can help you find him?"

**2** My beloved has gone down to his garden, to browse among the beds of spices. He is grazing in the gardens, gathering lilies.

**3** I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine. He browses among the lilies.

**4** You are beautiful, my darling, like the lovely city of Tirzah, yes, as beautiful as Jerusalem, as majestic as an army with flying banners.

**5** Turn your eyes away from me; they overpower me! Your hair falls in waves like a flock of goats coming down from Gilead.

**6** Your teeth are as white as sheep that are freshly washed; each one has its perfect match, and none is missing.

**7** Your cheeks behind your veil are like rosy halves of pomegranate.

**8** Even among sixty queens and eighty concubines and countless young women, **9** I would still choose my dove, my perfect one — the only daughter of her mother, the favorite of the one who bore her. The young women see her and call her blessed; even queens and concubines sing her praises:

**10** "Who is this, arising like the dawn, as fair as the moon, as bright as the sun, as majestic as an army with banners?"

**11** I went down to the walnut grove and out to the valley to see the new spring growth, to see whether the grapevines had budded or the pomegranates were in bloom.

**12** Before I realized it, my desire had taken me to the royal chariots of my people.

**13** Come back, come back, O Shulammite; come back, come back, that we may look at you! Why do you stare at the Shulammite, as at the dance of the two camps?

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**"I am my beloved's and my beloved is mine" (v.3):** This is the Song's second mutual possession formula (compare 2:16). The order has reversed — she now places her belonging to him first. The relationship has matured from claiming ("he is mine") to giving ("I am his").

**The Shulammite (v.13):** This is the only place in the Song where the woman is given a name or title. "Shulammite" may connect her to Shunem (the hometown of the beautiful Abishag, 1 Kings 1:3) or may be a feminine form of "Solomon" — making her his perfect counterpart.

*-- PNEUMA*
